Privacy policy · updated 13 Oct 2026

What happens to your days

Kai’s Flow is a journal. This page says, in plain words, what it keeps, who else sees any of it, and how to take it all back.

§1What we keep

Your account email, and what you put in the app: tasks, projects, calendar blocks, routines, your journal, the people you add, books, notes and quotes. It lives in a database run by Supabase, in the EU (Frankfurt). Each account can read only its own rows. We open the database only to keep the service running, or when you ask us to.

The app also keeps a working copy of your tasks and plans on your device so it opens and works offline. Your journal, notes about people and the Trash are left out of that copy.

Photos of your handwritten pages (Paper capture) are kept for 7 days so you can look back at them, then deleted — or within the hour after you review them, if you choose that in Settings.

When a new version of the app is released, a copy of the database is saved to private storage in case something goes wrong. Only the 14 newest copies are kept: each new one clears the oldest. So something you delete stays in those copies until 14 more versions have come out, and then it’s gone.

In short: your email and your days, in the EU.

§2What the AI sees

What you capture in the app — typed, spoken, or a photo of your notes — so it can pick out the date, the time and the rest; and a message in chat, with the items from your account it looks up to answer you. We send these to Groq, which doesn’t train on them and, with zero data retention, keeps nothing after replying. Search inside the app runs in our own database, not through an AI company. Things sent to your capture link stay away from the AI unless you ask, and nothing else in your account goes to Groq.

If you connect an AI assistant of your own with a key from Settings, it reads your tasks, projects, calendar and Inbox notes through that key — never your journal or the people you keep — and its maker’s policy covers what it sees. Turn the key off and it stops at once.

Only what you hand it, and it forgets.

§3Google Calendar

Only if you connect it in Settings, Kai’s Flow reads the events of the Google calendars you choose (read-only access) and shows them on your calendar beside your tasks, so you can plan around them. It never changes, adds to or deletes anything in your Google Calendar. The events are kept in your account like your own blocks, refreshed every 15 minutes; disconnect any time from Settings and they’re removed along with the access. We don’t use your calendar for anything else, sell it, or show it to anyone, and it isn’t sent to the AI. Kai’s Flow’s use of information received from Google APIs will adhere to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

Read to show, never to change.

§4What we never do

No ads. No selling or sharing your data. No tracking, analytics or fingerprinting, in the app or on this site. This site sets no cookies; the app keeps you signed in with your browser’s own storage.

To work at all, a few services see a little: Cloudflare serves the app and this site, and sees your IP address like any web host. This site loads its fonts from Google Fonts and asks GitHub for the newest version number, so your browser talks to those two as well.

Nothing to sell.

§5Taking it with you, or leaving

There’s no export button yet. Write to us and we’ll send you everything you’ve written, as plain files — or delete your account and everything in it from the database. Things you put in the Trash are deleted for good after 30 days.

Ask, and it’s yours. Or gone.

§6Talking to us

Write to [contact email]. Kai’s Flow is made by one person, Kai, and he reads every message. If this policy changes, the date at the top changes and Field notes says what moved.

A person answers.
